body.heading: Counting is naming numbers in order
paragraphs: Numbers have a special order, like steps on a staircase. Once you know the order, you can count anything: stones, stairs, strawberries, stars.
Count along with Mango. Point to your fingers, your toes — whatever helps!

body.heading: One to ten
paragraphs: 1 one, 2 two, 3 three, 4 four, 5 five, 6 six, 7 seven, 8 eight, 9 nine, 10 ten.
You have exactly ten fingers. Coincidence? Counting probably started with fingers, long, long ago!

body.heading: Eleven to twenty
paragraphs: 11 eleven, 12 twelve, 13 thirteen, 14 fourteen, 15 fifteen, 16 sixteen, 17 seventeen, 18 eighteen, 19 nineteen, 20 twenty.
See the pattern? After twelve, most numbers end in '-teen' — thirteen, fourteen, fifteen. They are the teenagers of numbers!

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Count the stairs in your home. How many are there — more than ten? More than twenty?
2. Count backwards from ten, like a rocket launch: 10, 9, 8… blast off!

takeaway: Numbers march in order from 1 to 20 — and after twelve, the '-teen' pattern (thirteen, fourteen, fifteen) helps you remember the way.
